sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and the State.

2. This is an application for bail U/s.438 Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioner in apprehension of arrest for her alleged involvement in the offences U/s. 406/420/506/34 of IPC.
3.

In view of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the Additional Standing Counsel, admittedly the parties did not pulling well subsequent to their marriage and a matrimonial dispute continued between them resulting allegations and counter allegation and the matter has also travelled to different forums.

Allegedly the Petitioner to have received a sum of Rs.
4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Only) i.e. Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) more than the amount that was agreed upon to be paid by the Informant to the Petitioner before the Mahila Commission.
Subsequently at the behest of the Informant a civil proceeding has also been filed before the Judge Family Court for the divorce.

Keeping in view the aforesaid back ground of the cases the question as to the money taken by the Petitioner beyond Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) could be settled before the matter in the Judge, Family Court.

sentences.text: Keeping in view the submission, the nature of allegations as emerged from the materials on record, the circumstances appearing, the seriousness and gravity of the offences, this Court is not inclined to grant the anticipatory bail

, however, it is directed that in the event the Petitioner surrenders and moves for bail in connection with G.R. Case No.160 of 2023 arising out of Kujang P.S. Case No.70 of 2023 pending in the court of learned J.M.F.C (P), Kujang, within a period of three weeks hence and she shall be admitted to bail on such terms and conditions as would be deemed just and proper by the said court with further conditions that the Petitioner shall appear in person before the learned court below on each date of posting of the case; shall appear before the I.O. once in a week till the submission of final form and shall cooperate with the investigation as and when required; shall not threaten, intimidate or terrorize the Informant; shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence in any manner whatsoever, while on bail.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
6. The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.
(Chittaranjan Dash) Judge BKSahoo Leena Rout vs State Of Odisha .... Opp.
